items.headline: TODAY: Tencent interim results — board also weighs an interim dividend; the stock fell 2.2% into the print
items.summary: Tencent's board meets today, 12 Aug 2026, to approve unaudited interim results for the six months to 30 June and to consider an interim dividend (HKEX notice, filed 23 Jun). TIMING — the notice does NOT state a release time; Tencent's customary practice is to release after the 16:00 HKT close, which would put the price reaction in Thursday's HK session. Treat that as inference, not a sourced fact. Into the print the stock closed Tuesday at HK$470.80, down 2.2% (implied prior close HK$481.40; 10.60/481.40 = -2.20%, internally consistent), named in the Hong Kong close report as one of the heavyweight tech drags. Not to be confused with Tencent Music, which reported separately on 11 Aug. LIMIT: the sell-side preview page (IG) returned HTTP 403, so NO revenue or net-profit consensus figure is carried here — treat any consensus number seen elsewhere as unverified.
items.actionable: The market de-risked ahead of the number rather than positioning for a beat — a 2.2% give-back the session before results. Any pre-positioning has to happen this afternoon SGT or not at all. Note the collision: Tencent lands around the 16:00 HKT close and US July CPI at 20:30 SGT, so a hedge sized for one event is exposed to the other.

items.headline: TONIGHT 20:30 SGT: US July CPI — consensus is disinflationary (3.4% headline / 2.5% core) yet September is priced ~50/50 for a HIKE
items.summary: NOT YET RELEASED — due Wednesday 12 Aug 08:30 ET = 20:30 SGT tonight, independently confirmed on the BLS release schedule. CONSENSUS: headline 3.4% y/y easing from 3.5%; core 2.5% y/y easing from 2.6%. The month-over-month forecast range previously circulating here has been REMOVED — no loaded source carried it, so it is not reported. The tension is that consensus points down while September fed-funds pricing sits at roughly a coin flip between a hike and a hold, versus 67% odds of a hike a week ago (CME FedWatch, per the 11 Aug report). Two Tuesday inputs cut opposite ways: NFIB pricing intentions fell hard (below), while NFIB hiring plans rebounded against Friday's -23,000 payrolls. And a two-session $5 move in crude feeds inflation expectations hours before the print.
items.actionable: An in-line or soft print is largely priced and mildly supportive for metals and the rate-sensitive SGX names. The tail that matters is a HOT print: it would spike hike odds, push the 30Y through 5.254% into today's $42bn 10-year auction, and hit the 1.6x levered silver hardest of anything in the book. Check margin headroom BEFORE 20:30 SGT, not after.

items.headline: Hammack: multiple hikes may be needed — a 2026 voter who already dissented for a hike argues 3.50-3.75% is not restrictive
items.summary: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, a 2026 voter who dissented at the July FOMC in favour of a 25bp INCREASE (one of three who did), told Yahoo Finance that multiple rate increases will likely be needed to stop inflation becoming entrenched, declining to specify how many. Verbatim: 'I would say in general, one 25-basis-point move probably doesn't do a whole lot for the economy... So it's probably some number of [movements].' On the stance: the current 3.50-3.75% range is not 'meaningfully restricting' the economy — 'When I'm talking to businesses, I'm not hearing that they're sensing any restraint from investments in growth based on where interest rates are.' She added: 'Nothing would make me feel better than to be wrong.' TIMING CORRECTION: the Fox Business report is stamped 11 Aug 15:58 ET — two minutes before the cash close — and gives no time for the interview itself, so this CANNOT be claimed to have driven Tuesday's session. The '45% Monday' and 'above 60% pre-payrolls' figures previously carried have been dropped; neither appears in any loaded source. The Fed is chaired by Kevin Warsh, sworn in 22 May 2026.
items.actionable: The September distribution contains no cut at all — the debate is hike versus hold, and a voting member is arguing for a multi-hike sequence. Rising real-rate expectations are the textbook headwind for non-yielding metals, and the silver position is levered 1.6x on IBKR margin, so drawdowns compound against a margin base.

items.headline: NFIB small-business optimism jumps to 99.8, highest since Aug 2025 — but pricing intentions FALL sharply
items.summary: The NFIB Small Business Optimism Index rose 2.4 points in July to 99.8, above its 52-year average of 98.0 and the highest since August 2025, versus consensus of about 97.5. Eight of ten components rose. Hiring contributed most: net 20% plan new jobs over the next three months, up 9 points and the highest since October 2022; the NFIB Employment Index is 102.1 and 36% report unfilled openings, up 4 points. The Uncertainty Index rose 2 to 91 against a 68 average. THE INFLATION COMPONENTS ARE THE STORY: net 31% raised average selling prices, DOWN 7 points from June; net 28% plan increases in the next three months, DOWN 4; and only 14% cite inflation as their single biggest problem, DOWN 7 and the first decline this year. Labour quality replaced it at 27%, up 8.
items.actionable: Genuinely two-sided hours before CPI. The hiring rebound contradicts Friday's -23,000 July payrolls, which is what knocked September hike odds down in the first place — hawkish. But the pricing components are unambiguously disinflationary and lead core goods CPI reasonably well, supporting tonight's soft consensus. For levered silver the disinflation half is the more relevant one: it says the inflation-hedge bid is not being refreshed by actual price-setting behaviour.

items.headline: $58bn 3-year auction clears at 4.291% with above-average demand — but the $42bn 10-year prices AFTER tonight's CPI
items.summary: Treasury sold $58bn of 3-year notes Tuesday at a 4.291% high yield with a 2.71 bid-to-cover, above the 2.64 average of the prior ten auctions. July's comparable cleared at 4.179% with 2.60 cover — so investors absorbed a HIGHER yield AND showed BETTER cover. This is leg one of the August refunding: $42bn of 10-years today at 13:00 ET (about 4.5 hours after CPI) and $25bn of 30-years Thursday, $125bn total. VERIFICATION NOTE: a search snippet reported this as '$42bn at 3.202%, cover 2.50' — that is wrong, conflated with a stale 2024-era auction. The article says $58bn/4.291%/2.71, and $58+$42+$25 reconciles exactly to the $125bn refunding.
items.actionable: Solid front-end demand at a higher clearing yield is the most plausible reason the long end held rather than extending on Tuesday. The sequencing is the risk: today's 10-year auction prices AFTER the CPI release, so a hot print forces dealers to underwrite $42bn of supply into a selloff — the specific mechanism that would push the 30Y decisively through 5.254% and mark down the S-REIT sleeve.

items.headline: Silver reverses hard: seven-week high near $66 in Asia, closes ~$64.71-64.73 spot, -1.5% — the largest single-day drag on the levered position
items.summary: Spot silver rose to a seven-week high around $66/oz in Asian hours tracking gold, then sold off through the US session. Two feeds: $64.7065 (Investing.com XAG/USD) and $64.733 (Trading Economics) — a 2.6-cent spread. VERIFICATION done manually because the vendor prints disagreed: Trading Economics shows -$0.97 (-1.48%), implying a $65.70 previous close, matching Monday's published $65.714 to within 1.4 cents; Investing.com independently lists its previous close as exactly $64.7065, confirming the Tuesday level on a second feed. Computed off Monday's published $65.714 the move is -$1.0075 or -1.53%. So: -1.48% on TE's own print, -1.53% on Investing's, and both reconcile to Monday. LABELLING: spot has no official close — these are end-of-Tuesday levels read around 19:40-19:45 ET, not a struck settlement. A Yahoo piece quoting September futures opening at $65.94 'up 1%' is a morning-only reading and does not describe the day. Trading Economics attributed the reversal to profit-taking and to traders reassessing how the oil spike feeds inflation and Fed policy. Structural note from the same page: Chinese imports of silver-bearing ores rose 62.5% y/y in June to 219,000 tonnes.
items.actionable: At 1.6x IBKR margin a -1.5% spot move is roughly -2.4% on the position, and the intraday round trip from ~$66.30 to $64.71 is the kind of range that moves maintenance margin even when the close looks orderly. The setup into tonight — rejected at a seven-week high, oil up 5% in two sessions, positioning long into an inflation print — is a configuration where a hot number cuts both ways. Flagging mechanics, not advising size.

items.headline: Gold spikes to a two-month high of $4,432.74 then closes DOWN at ~$4,368 (-0.5%) — a failed breakout, not a rally
items.summary: Widely-syndicated Tuesday headlines said 'gold gains for a third session' and 'gold remains over $4,400' — both were written off morning data and both are wrong about the day. Spot gold gained 1% to $4,432.74/oz by 02:17 GMT, its highest since 5 June, then gave the entire move back: $4,368.04 (-$23.30, -0.53%) on Trading Economics, $4,368.29 (-$23.05, -0.52%) on the second read. VERIFICATION: implied previous close $4,368.04 + $23.30 = $4,391.34, an EXACT match to Monday's published spot gold, so the percentage is clean; the Investing.com XAU/USD page shows a previous close of $4,368.15, agreeing within 11 cents. Context from the wire on what drove the morning bid: FOMO after the missed $4,000 dip, short-covering, safe-haven flows and continued Chinese institutional and central-bank accumulation.
items.actionable: The shape matters more than the level. Gold made a two-month high and could not hold it on a day when oil rose 1.4% and the 30Y sits at 2007 highs — normally a supportive backdrop. A rejection at $4,432 with a lower close is a materially different signal from a quiet -0.5% drift. Everything resets on tonight's CPI.

The clean test comes if CPI drives gold up tonight — that is when it becomes clear whether the lag was a signal about the miners or just noise.

items.headline: Oil extends the Hormuz surge — Brent SETTLES $88.91 (+1.4%), WTI $83.20 — even as Qatar says Oman-Iran talks are at an "advanced stage"
items.summary: Brent rose $1.19 (+1.4%) to settle $88.91; WTI rose $1.07 (+1.3%) to $83.20 — one-week highs and a fifth straight session of gains. So the standing question 'did Brent give back the 5% surge' is answered: it extended it. CORRECTION TO OUR OWN PUBLISHED MONDAY FIGURES: the implied previous closes here are $87.72 and $82.13, which do NOT match the $87.85/$82.30 we published for Monday. Checked rather than assumed — two independent documents confirm Monday's actual exchange SETTLEMENTS were Brent $87.72 (+$4.19, +4.99%) and WTI $82.13 (+$3.95, +5.06%). The figures we published Monday were spot/CFD quotes, ~13-17 cents high, not settlements. Against our published numbers Tuesday computes to +$1.06 (+1.21%) Brent and +$0.90 (+1.09%) WTI; against the true settles, +1.4% and +1.3%. Separately Investing.com's Brent futures page currently shows +$1.58 (+1.80%) — that change is referenced to Monday's $87.72 and its 'prev. close' field reads $88.96 against the wire's $88.91; the Reuters settlement language was used. DRIVER: doubt that a US-Iran deal will quickly restore flows. Hormuz transits fell to six vessels Monday against a 10-day average of ~11 and a pre-war 125-140 daily; crude and product net exports through the strait averaged 3.0m bpd in the week to 7 Aug, down from 4.4m bpd. THE DIPLOMACY, SAME DAY: at the Qatari foreign ministry briefing Tuesday, spokesman Dr Majed bin Mohammed al-Ansari said Oman-Iran negotiations on Hormuz shipping have reached an advanced stage and called this a watershed moment in US-Iran negotiations; the minimum threshold at this stage is restoring freedom of navigation under international law, and Doha wants the strait reopened immediately. DATING CAVEATS BOTH WAYS: the widely-quoted line that the strait "will not open until America corrects its behavior" is from Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, reported as an IRGC commander conveying a Supreme National Security Council message with six conditions, and dates to Saturday 8 Aug — it is being recycled in Tuesday copy. And the Oman-Iran agreement on proposed route coordinates was announced by Iran on 5 Aug, not Tuesday. The genuinely new Tuesday item is the Qatari briefing alone.
items.actionable: Supportive for the oil sleeve, and a second leg rather than a one-day spike. The wider read-through matters more: a $5 two-session move in crude feeds straight into inflation expectations hours before tonight's CPI, the pivot for the whole metals-and-rates side of the book. Watch whether Brent holds $88 through the print. AND THE TWO-SIDED RISK: crude settling at one-week highs on the very day the mediator says a deal is close means the market is pricing scepticism — so gap risk is asymmetric to the downside on any concrete announcement, and a Hormuz reopening would hit the oil sleeve AND remove a chunk of the safe-haven bid under silver at the same time, a correlated drawdown against the 1.6x levered position. A Tehran announcement could land in the same window as tonight's CPI.

items.headline: SGX reopens and RALLIES: STI +0.98% to 5,754.17 despite the 5.254% 30Y, with MTI upgrading 2026 GDP to 4.5-5.5% and OCBC at a record
items.summary: The STI closed 5,754.17, +55.74 (+0.98%). VERIFICATION: SGX was shut Monday 10 Aug for National Day, so the reference is FRIDAY 7 Aug's 5,698.43 — not Monday. Computed manually: 5,754.17 - 5,698.43 = 55.74, and 55.74/5,698.43 = +0.978%, matching the quoted +0.98%; the Investing.com historical table has NO 10 Aug row at all, which independently confirms the holiday. Session traded 5,667.05-5,774.21 off a 5,695.18 open, closing near the high. THE MACRO: MTI on 11 Aug upgraded its 2026 GDP forecast to 4.5-5.5% from 2.0-4.0%, citing better-than-expected H1 and accelerating global AI-related capex; Q2 GDP +5.9% y/y and +1.4% q/q SA, H1 +6.1% y/y — all four read directly on MTI's own release. LEADERS: Yangzijiang +9.1%, OCBC +3.5-3.8%, Hongkong Land +2.5%, DBS +0.9-1.0%, Singtel +0.23%. FEED DISCREPANCY ON OCBC, declared rather than smoothed over: a post-close quote timestamped 11 Aug 17:15:33 SGT shows S$31.36 (+3.50%), while the STI constituents table shows a 31.43 close (+3.8%) with a 30.10-31.56 day range against a 52-week high of 31.56 — i.e. a record high either way, but the exact close is 31.36 vs 31.43 depending on feed. Both reconcile off the same S$30.30 prior close. DBS closed S$76.99 (+0.86%) at 17:13:58 SGT. OCBC's Q2 was reported Thursday 6 Aug, NOT Tuesday — net profit S$2.22bn (+22% y/y, first quarter above S$2bn), H1 S$4.19bn (+13%), NIM 1.70% (-22bp y/y), interim dividend 47 cents (+15%), wealth AUM a record S$350bn, FY26 loan growth guided up to high-single/low-double digit, S$2.5bn capital return targeted by FY26. Because Monday was a holiday only TWO sessions have traded since that result. A reported 17 Aug ex-date for the S$0.47 dividend appears on a timestamped data page but is NOT confirmed against OCBC's own filing.
items.actionable: The feared long-end-yield repricing of Singapore did not show up on day one — the sleeve marked UP on the reopen, and an AI-capex-led 4.5-5.5% GDP year favours the banks over the REITs. IMPORTANT LABELLING: every SGX percent change here spans Friday-to-Tuesday and embeds three calendar days of offshore news including the Hormuz oil spike — these are not clean single-session moves. OCBC at a record on a 22% profit beat that is now two sessions old is the concrete trim-or-hold decision in the sleeve.

items.actionable: The developer/REIT split is the shape to watch: with the 30Y at 5.254%, developers rallied and the trusts did not follow. If the 0.00% prints are real, this sleeve is the part of the SGX book genuinely failing to participate — and since three peer REITs moved on the same table, it is name-specific rather than a rates story. Worth a direct check against your broker marks today; this item does not meet the verification standard of the rest of the brief. Wing Tai remains unconfirmed.

On 26,662 Xiaomi units the HK$0.96 fall is roughly HK$25,600 of mark-to-market in one session, and at -3.5% Xiaomi underperformed even HS Tech: stock-specific weakness on top of sector weakness. items.headline: DATA-INTEGRITY ALERT: Japan was CLOSED Tuesday for Mountain Day — no Nikkei close exists. Shanghai -0.82%, KOSPI +0.73%

Caught because the Nikkei historical table simply had no 11 August row despite covering the period, then confirmed at document level against a JPX 2026 trading-holiday calendar listing the exact row 'Tuesday | Aug 11, 2026 | Mountain Day | Full Day Off'. The last Nikkei close therefore remains Monday's 66,970.22. ELSEWHERE: Shanghai Composite 3,934.09, -32.50 (-0.82%) — implied previous close 3,966.59 matches our published Monday figure exactly. KOSPI 6,345.53, +45.87 (+0.73%) — implied previous close 6,299.66 matches Monday exactly. Both confirmed.
items.actionable: If any feed or app shows you a Tuesday Nikkei figure, it is Monday's 66,970.22 being re-served with a false date — precisely the stale-reference failure that has burned this dashboard repeatedly, except today it is guaranteed rather than merely possible. Korea at +0.73% diverged sharply from China and Hong Kong, so the Tuesday Asia tape was not uniformly risk-off: the weakness was specifically Greater China tech.
